mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.3%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS predicting 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index above 240 (CPIAUCSL) indicates elevated inflation, triggering monetary tightening expectations that increase discount rates and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 240, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL predicting 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS > 145000 and UNRATE < 4.5) indicates robust economic activity and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through joint labor market strength.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS > 145000 and UNRATE < 4.5, or the Rank IC for the joint signal predicting 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 > 16600 and HOUST > 1200), rising interest rate expectations compress profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through joint demand indicators.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 > 16600 and HOUST > 1200, or the Rank IC for the joint signal predicting 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 104 (INDPRO) signals supply chain contraction and recession risk, triggering equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 104, or the Rank IC for INDPRO predicting 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST > 1200) indicate strong consumer demand and economic momentum, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1200, or the Rank IC for HOUST predicting 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate below 4.5% (UNRATE) signals tight labor market conditions, increasing wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5, or the Rank IC for UNRATE predicting 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 0.5), higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite compress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS predicting 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
